issues.reason: The half that stands: the text never places the approving itself at the Harbor Station, and the favored reading restricts the half-shifts, so the atom commits to an unstated fact; the half that does not: Thematic roles licenses `Location` for an 'at'-PP answering 'where' on the event, that is the default attachment, and the competing site has no licensed carrier here (a bare-kind `half_shift` Theme cannot take a place atom), so this is at least as much gap territory as parser error.

The half that stands: Core patterns forbids this atom by name — 'a wick sits in a lantern ... must not yield (PartOf sk_wick_1 sk_lantern_1)'; the half that does not: the claim that no words put it there is refuted by the Bridging bullet of Coreference & anaphora, which licenses exactly this definite-part-to-antecedent `PartOf` (and extends it even within one sentence), so the parse is caught between two contradictory rules rather than asserting something untrue of the passage.

Thematic roles' single test — does the object itself change? — puts deposited-unchanged threads in `Theme` (the moved/displaced line, and the 'slid the plate off the counter' motion-result precedent), and the same section says default to `Theme` when unclear, so `Patient` mis-slots the role and breaks the statement/question role agreement the test exists to guarantee.

gaps_confirmed: 'for the first time' — an occasion-count adverbial on an episodic event has no carrier: `Ordinal` ranks entities, `Again` presupposes a prior same-type event (the opposite claim), and nothing else records a first occurrence.

coordinated temporal adjunct PPs on one verb ('at midnight and at the third watch') — Coordination & plurals covers coordinated clauses/VPs and argument NPs, never adjuncts, so nothing says whether the event replicates; two `Time` atoms on one event would assert a contradiction, so the parser's two join events are the sound improvisation.
new_gaps: A locative restriction on a kind-level role filler ('approved half-shifts ... at the Harbor Station') has no licensed form: `LocatedIn` takes an entity — Conditional properties explicitly bars putting a kind in its entity slot — and the preposition-named oblique attaches to events or entities, not kinds, so carrying the restriction would force the bare-kind object into a group witness that nothing licenses either.

Core patterns ('a wick sits in a lantern ... must not yield (PartOf sk_wick_1 sk_lantern_1)') and the Bridging bullet ('Alice bought a car. The engine was broken' -> (PartOf sk_engine_1 sk_car_1), bridged 'the same way' inside one sentence) give flatly opposite instructions for the same construction; a licensed form has to state whether a bridged definite part carries its `PartOf` anchor or stays unanchored.

A non-Gregorian day-count date ('day 80 of Year 1') has no term: `(Day <n>)` is the day-of-month slot, so a day-of-year ordinal silently reuses a slot that means something else, and nothing distinguishes the two readings at query time.
defect_summary: The compliant form for the confirmed issue is `(Theme sk_leave_1 sk_threads_1)` — 'left silken threads on the lantern' displaces the threads without altering them, so the change test and its unclear-case default both give `Theme`; on the partials, no licensed form exists for the favored 'half-shifts at the Harbor Station' reading (the gap above), and the instruction set licenses both emitting and forbidding the wick `PartOf`, so it licenses no single compliant form there either.
notes: Both partials are instruction-set problems rather than parser lapses — one attachment whose favored site has no carrier, one atom that Core patterns forbids and Bridging mandates. The rest of the parse checks out: the postural `(Past (Beside pell coraline_ash))`, the `So` + `Before` pair over the two past perfects, the compound decompositions (`nightmoth`/`silken_thread`/`senior_keeper`, with noun modifiers left unexposed), the `TimeAtLeast` for 'after sundown', and the bare-plural group witnesses.
